Channels
chăn´ĕlz
n. pl. (the beds of watercourses; the deep courses of the sea — Hebrew aphiq)
Latin canalis, a pipe or groove, through Old French chanel. The Hebrew aphiq means a containing channel — the bed that holds a stream, and by extension anything strong and confining.

Biblical Definition

Channels are the beds of waters, and Scripture shows them laid bare by the breath of God. David's song of deliverance: “the channels of the sea appeared, the foundations of the world were discovered, at the rebuking of the LORD, at the blast of the breath of his nostrils” (2Sa 22:16); the psalm repeats it: “Then the channels of waters were seen, and the foundations of the world were discovered at thy rebuke, O LORD, at the blast of the breath of thy nostrils” (Psa 18:15). The picture is of the sea driven back to its floor by a word, as at the Red Sea. What a man cannot see, because it lies under the whole weight of the ocean, is uncovered by God's breath as easily as dust is blown from a table. Isaiah uses the same word for a flood of a different sort: Assyria is a river rising over its banks, “he shall come up over all his channels, and go over all his banks” (Isa 8:7), and “he shall pass through Judah; he shall overflow and go over, he shall reach even to the neck; and the stretching out of his wings shall fill the breadth of thy land, O Immanuel” (Isa 8:8). The invasion rises to the neck and no further, and the chapter halts it with a name — Immanuel, God with us.

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster (1828) defines a channel as the hollow bed of a river or stream of water; a canal; the deeper part of a strait, bay or harbor.

expand to see more

CHAN'NEL, n. In a general sense, a passage; a place of passing or flowing; particularly, the place where a river flows, including the whole breadth of the river.

2. The deeper part of a strait, bay or harbor, where the main current flows.

3. That through which any thing passes; means of passing, conveying or transmitting.

BANK, n. The margin of a watercourse; the rising ground bordering a river.

Key Scripture

Psalm 18:15 — "Then the channels of waters were seen, and the foundations of the world were discovered at thy rebuke, O LORD, at the blast of the breath of thy nostrils."

2 Samuel 22:16 — "And the channels of the sea appeared, the foundations of the world were discovered, at the rebuking of the LORD, at the blast of the breath of his nostrils."

Isaiah 8:7 — "Now therefore, behold, the Lord bringeth up upon them the waters of the river, strong and many, even the king of Assyria, and all his glory: and he shall come up over all his channels, and go over all his banks:"

Isaiah 8:8 — "And he shall pass through Judah; he shall overflow and go over, he shall reach even to the neck; and the stretching out of his wings shall fill the breadth of thy land, O Immanuel."

Modern Corruption

Empires and disasters are read as forces in their own right, when Isaiah says plainly that the Lord brings up the river and fixes how far it rises.

expand to see more

Isaiah 8:7 does not say Assyria rose against Judah; it says the Lord bringeth up upon them the waters of the river, even the king of Assyria. The empire is the instrument; the hand is God's. This is the harder half of providence and the church has always found ways round it — God permitted, God allowed, God did not prevent. Scripture uses the active voice. And the same sentence that gives the flood its author gives it its limit: it reaches to the neck. A river that God brings does not drown the people God keeps, and the chapter names the reason in a single word, Immanuel.

The psalms of deliverance make the same point from the other direction. When God rebukes, the channels of the sea appear and the foundations of the world are uncovered — that is, what is deepest, most hidden, and most permanent in creation is laid open by His breath. Every account of the world in which its underlying structures are simply there, immovable and unaddressed, is answered by this image. The believer's comfort is not that the waters are shallow but that the One who made the channels is the One who commands them.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Hebrew aphiq (H650), a channel, watercourse, or strong containing bed — 2 Samuel 22:16, Psalm 18:15, Isaiah 8:7, Psalm 42:1 of the water brooks.

expand to see more

Hebrew aphiq (H650) — a channel or watercourse; 2 Samuel 22:16, Psalm 18:15, Psalm 42:1, Ezekiel 6:3.

Hebrew mosad (H4146) — foundation; the companion word, the foundations of the world uncovered.

Hebrew gaarah (H1606) — a rebuke; what dries the channels, as at the Red Sea.

Hebrew ruach appo — the breath of his nostrils; the same phrase used in Exodus 15:8 of the sea standing upright.

Isaiah 8:8 fixes the flood's limit at the neck, and names the reason: O Immanuel.

Usage

"“The channels of the sea appeared… at the blast of the breath of his nostrils”."

"“The Lord bringeth up upon them the waters of the river” — the active voice."

"“He shall reach even to the neck” — and no further, O Immanuel."
